The body generates no new data: it has no Methods section, no animal ethics statement (instead 'There are no ethical issues related to this review article'), and every experimental statement is attributed to other laboratories. Per instruction, no PK values were harvested. For transparency about what was deliberately NOT extracted: the body cites, from other papers, an in vitro half-life for acylated apelin-13 analogues of '24 hours vs >2.1 hours' for native apelin-13, and states that 'Lys GluPAL(Tyr )apelin-13 had an in vivo half-life of 2.5 to 3 hours'; it also mentions qualitatively that pGlu-apelin-13 'has a longer half-life' than apelin-13 and that native apelin-13 has a 'short biological half-life'. These are third-party findings reported by the review, not findings of this article, so they were not entered as agent-level PK. Likewise the many doses quoted in the body (e.g. 25 nmol/kg bw apelin-13 analogues, 2 mg/kg (pGlu)apelin-13 osmotic pump, 9 or 30 nmol/kg bw in 16 overweight men) all belong to cited studies, so no agent objects were created. study_types is recorded as ['review'] because none of the protocol's clinical / in vivo / ex vivo / in vitro categories describes work performed by these authors. Table 1 does print apelin isoform sequences (e.g. apelin-13 QRPRLSHKGPMPF, apelin-17 KFRRQRPRLSHKGPMPF), which matches the PEPLIFE2 metadata peptides, but as the review dosed nothing these were not turned into agent entries.

The only half-life in the body, 3.6 h, comes from incubating the peptide in serum harvested from a CPC;Apc mouse at 37 °C and following it by RP-HPLC over 24 h. It is a proteolytic stability half-life measured ex vivo, not a plasma elimination half-life from a dosed animal, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and both half_life_absorption and half_life_elimination are 'not reported'. The paper's own section heading 'In Vivo Serum Stability' is misleading relative to its Methods; the matrix field records the assay as it was actually performed. The in vivo pharmacokinetics section is entirely imaging-based: 'Quantified intensities showed a peak T/B ratio at 1 h after injection of QQT*-IRDye800. Human involvement was limited to donor-derived colonoid tissue (adenoma from a 46-year-old male and a 64-year-old male, normal colon from a 43-year-old female deceased donor) cultured in vitro; no human subject was dosed, so clinical_detail is null.
